What is Spring: Spring is a comprehensive Java framework for building enterprise applications. Spring Boot simplifies Spring development with auto-configuration, embedded servers, and starter dependencies. Key modules: Spring Core (DI/IoC), Spring MVC (web), Spring Data (databases), Spring Security (auth), Spring Cloud (microservices). Spring Boot's opinionated defaults reduce boilerplate while remaining configurable. Convention over configuration with auto-configuration classes. Starter POMs bundle related dependencies.

<!-- pom.xml - Spring Boot starter -->
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project>
    <parent>
        <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
        <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-parent</artifactId>
        <version>3.2.0</version>
    </parent>
    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
    <artifactId>demo</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0</version>
    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>
    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
                <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

// Main application class
package com.example.demo;
import org.springframework.boot.SpringApplication;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.SpringBootApplication;

@SpringBootApplication
public class DemoApplication {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        SpringApplication.run(DemoApplication.class, args);
    }
}

// Run: mvn spring-boot:run
// Or: java -jar target/demo-1.0.0.jar
Project Structure: Spring Boot projects follow a layered architecture. Typical structure: controller (REST endpoints), service (business logic), repository (data access), model/entity (domain objects), dto (data transfer objects), config (configuration classes), exception (custom exceptions), util (utilities). Resources folder contains application.yml, static files, and templates. The @SpringBootApplication main class is typically at the root package. Package structure by feature or by layer.

src/
├── main/java/com/example/demo/
│   ├── DemoApplication.java
│   ├── config/
│   │   ├── SecurityConfig.java
│   │   └── SwaggerConfig.java
│   ├── controller/
│   │   └── UserController.java
│   ├── service/
│   │   ├── UserService.java
│   │   └── impl/UserServiceImpl.java
│   ├── repository/
│   │   └── UserRepository.java
│   ├── model/
│   │   └── User.java

Configuration: Spring Boot externalizes configuration via application.properties or application.yml. YAML is more readable for hierarchical config. Profile-specific files: application-dev.yml, application-prod.yml. Active profiles via spring.profiles.active. Custom properties with @ConfigurationProperties (type-safe). @Value for simple injection. Environment variables override properties. Random values with ${random.int}. Command-line args override file properties. Spring Cloud Config for centralized config.

Spring IoC: Inversion of Control (IoC) is Spring's core - the container manages object creation and wiring. Annotations: @Component, @Service, @Repository, @Controller, @RestController register beans. @Autowired injects dependencies (by type). @Primary resolves conflicts when multiple beans of same type. @Qualifier specifies exact bean. @Bean for explicit declaration in @Configuration classes. @Scope controls bean lifecycle (singleton, prototype, request, session). @PostConstruct and @PreDestroy for lifecycle callbacks.

REST Controllers: @RestController combines @Controller + @ResponseBody for REST APIs. Request mapping annotations: @GetMapping, @PostMapping, @PutMapping, @DeleteMapping, @PatchMapping. Extract data with: @PathVariable, @RequestParam, @RequestBody, @RequestHeader. @Valid for request validation. ResponseEntity for full HTTP response control. @ExceptionHandler for controller-level exception handling. @InitBinder for custom data binding.
Exception Handling: Global exception handling with @ControllerAdvice. @ExceptionHandler for specific exceptions. Custom error response DTO for consistent API errors. HTTP status code mapping: 400 (bad request), 404 (not found), 409 (conflict), 500 (internal error). Field-level validation errors with MethodArgumentNotValidException. ResponseEntityExceptionHandler provides default Spring exceptions.

JPA Entities: Spring Data JPA simplifies database access. Entities are POJOs with @Entity annotation. @Table customizes table name. @Id + @GeneratedValue for primary keys. @Column for column customization. Relationships: @OneToOne, @OneToMany, @ManyToOne, @ManyToMany. @JoinColumn for foreign key. Cascade types: ALL, PERSIST, MERGE, REMOVE. Fetch types: LAZY (default for collections), EAGER. @Embeddable for value objects. @Enumerated for enums. @PrePersist/@PreUpdate for lifecycle callbacks.
Spring Data Repositories: Spring Data JPA generates implementations at runtime. Extend JpaRepository<T, ID> for full CRUD. Custom query methods via method naming: findBy, findByFieldNameContaining, findByFieldNameBetween, countBy, existsBy. @Query for custom JPQL/SQL. @Modifying + @Transactional for update/delete. Specifications for dynamic queries. Projections for partial data. @EntityGraph for eager fetching. Pageable for pagination.

Building REST APIs: Spring Boot makes building REST APIs straightforward. Use @RestController with request mappings. Content negotiation via produces/consumes. HATEOAS with links for discoverability. Versioning via URL, header, or content type. CORS with @CrossOrigin or global config. HTTP method support: GET (read), POST (create), PUT (replace), PATCH (partial update), DELETE (remove). @Valid for request body validation. DTOs to decouple API from entities.
API Documentation: Springdoc OpenAPI generates API documentation automatically. Add springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui dependency. Access at /swagger-ui.html and /v3/api-docs. Customize with @OpenAPIDefinition, @Info, @Tag, @Operation, @ApiResponse. Group APIs with GroupedOpenApi. Spring Boot 3.x uses springdoc v2. Configuration via application.yml. OAuth2 security scheme definition. Request/response examples with @Schema.

<!-- pom.xml -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springdoc</groupId>
    <artifactId>springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui</artifactId>
    <version>2.3.0</version>
</dependency>

// Custom OpenAPI config
@Configuration
public class OpenApiConfig {
    @Bean
    public OpenAPI customOpenAPI() {
        return new OpenAPI()
            .info(new Info()
                .title("User API")
                .version("1.0.0")
                .description("REST API for user management"))
            .addSecurityItem(new SecurityRequirement()
                .addList("bearerAuth"))
            .components(new Components()
                .addSecuritySchemes("bearerAuth",
                    new SecurityScheme()
                        .type(SecurityScheme.Type.HTTP)
                        .scheme("bearer")
                        .bearerFormat("JWT")));
    }
}

// Controller annotations
@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/users")
@Tag(name = "Users", description = "User management endpoints")
public class UserController {
    @Operation(summary = "Get user by ID", description = "Returns a single user")
    @ApiResponse(responseCode = "200", description = "Found the user")
    @ApiResponse(responseCode = "404", description = "User not found")
    @GetMapping("/{id}")
    public ResponseEntity<UserResponse> get(@PathVariable Long id) { ... }
}

springdoc:
  swagger-ui:
    path: /swagger-ui.html
  api-docs:
    path: /v3/api-docs

Spring Security: Spring Security provides authentication, authorization, and protection against common attacks. Add spring-boot-starter-security dependency. Core concepts: SecurityFilterChain (filter pipeline), AuthenticationManager (auth processing), UserDetailsService (user lookup), PasswordEncoder (password hashing). @EnableMethodSecurity for method-level security with @PreAuthorize, @PostAuthorize, @Secured. CSRF protection (enabled by default for non-REST, disable for REST APIs with stateless JWT). CORS, headers, and exception handling configured in SecurityFilterChain bean.
JWT Authentication: JWT (JSON Web Token) is commonly used for stateless REST API authentication. Flow: User logs in with credentials, server validates and returns JWT token, client sends token in Authorization header on subsequent requests, server validates token on each request. Use io.jsonwebtoken (jjwt) library. JWT contains claims (sub, iat, exp, roles). Access tokens (short-lived) and refresh tokens (long-lived) pattern. Blacklist for token revocation.

Spring Boot Testing: Spring Boot provides comprehensive testing support. @SpringBootTest for integration tests. @WebMvcTest for controller layer (loads only web beans). @DataJpaTest for repository layer (in-memory DB). @MockBean for mocking dependencies. TestRestTemplate or MockMvc for HTTP testing. @TestContainers for real database integration tests. AssertJ for fluent assertions. Test slices reduce startup time by loading only relevant beans.

Actuator & Monitoring: Spring Boot Actuator provides production-ready monitoring and management endpoints. Add spring-boot-starter-actuator dependency. Key endpoints: /health (app health), /info (app info), /metrics (metrics), /env (environment), /loggers (logging levels), /httptrace (HTTP trace), /beans (all beans), /mappings (route mappings). Custom health indicators, metrics with Micrometer, and info contributors. Expose via HTTP or JMX. Integrate with Prometheus/Grafana for monitoring.

<!-- pom.xml -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-actuator</artifactId>
</dependency>
<dependency>
    <groupId>io.micrometer</groupId>
    <artifactId>micrometer-registry-prometheus</artifactId>
</dependency>

# application.yml
management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: health,info,metrics,env,loggers,prometheus
  endpoint:
    health:
      show-details: when-authorized
      show-components: when-authorized
  metrics:
    tags:
      application: ${spring.application.name}

// Custom health indicator
@Component
public class DatabaseHealthIndicator implements HealthIndicator {
    @Autowired
    private DataSource dataSource;

    @Override
    public Health health() {
        try (Connection conn = dataSource.getConnection()) {
            if (conn.isValid(1000)) {
                return Health.up().withDetail("database", "PostgreSQL").build();
            }
            return Health.down().withDetail("reason", "Connection timeout").build();
        } catch (Exception e) {
            return Health.down(e).build();
        }
    }
}

// Custom metrics
@Component
public class CustomMetrics {
    private final Counter userCreatedCounter;

    public CustomMetrics(MeterRegistry registry) {
        userCreatedCounter = Counter.builder("users.created")
            .description("Number of created users")
            .register(registry);
    }

    public void incrementUserCreated() {
        userCreatedCounter.increment();
    }
}
Profiles & Logging: Spring profiles activate different configurations per environment. Use @Profile on beans or profile-specific YAML/properties files. Set active profiles via spring.profiles.active. Logging with Logback (default). Configure levels per package: logging.level.com.example=DEBUG. Logback-spring.xml for advanced config. Logstash encoder for JSON logging (ELK stack). Distributed tracing with Micrometer Tracing + Zipkin. Structured logging for better observability.

# application.yml - logging
logging:
  level:
    com.example: DEBUG
    org.springframework: INFO
    org.hibernate.SQL: DEBUG
  pattern:
    console: "%d{yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss} [%thread] %-5level %logger{36} - %msg%n"
    file: "%d{yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss} [%thread] %-5level %logger{36} - %msg%n"
  file:
    name: logs/app.log
    max-size: 10MB
    max-history: 7

# logback-spring.xml - advanced
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<configuration>
    <appender name="CONSOLE" class="ch.qos.logback.core.ConsoleAppender">
        <encoder>
            <pattern>%d{HH:mm:ss.SSS} %-5level %logger{36} - %msg%n</pattern>
        </encoder>
    </appender>

    <appender name="FILE" class="ch.qos.logback.core.rolling.RollingFileAppender">
        <file>logs/app.log</file>
        <rollingPolicy class="ch.qos.logback.core.rolling.TimeBasedRollingPolicy">
            <fileNamePattern>logs/app-%d{yyyy-MM-dd}.log</fileNamePattern>
            <maxHistory>30</maxHistory>
        </rollingPolicy>
        <encoder>
            <pattern>%d{yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss} [%thread] %-5level %logger{36} - %msg%n</pattern>
        </encoder>
    </appender>

    <root level="INFO">
        <appender-ref ref="CONSOLE" />
        <appender-ref ref="FILE" />
    </root>

    <springProfile name="dev">
        <logger name="com.example" level="DEBUG" />
    </springProfile>

    <springProfile name="prod">
        <logger name="com.example" level="WARN" />
    </springProfile>
</configuration>

Spring Cloud: Spring Cloud provides tools for building microservices. Service discovery with Netflix Eureka or Consul. API Gateway with Spring Cloud Gateway. Load balancing with Spring Cloud LoadBalancer. Circuit breakers with Resilience4j. Distributed configuration with Spring Cloud Config. Distributed tracing with Micrometer + Zipkin. Event-driven communication with Spring Cloud Stream. Feign/WebClient for inter-service HTTP calls. Centralized logging with ELK stack.

WebFlux: Spring WebFlux provides reactive programming support for non-blocking, event-driven applications. Built on Project Reactor (Mono and Flux types). Reactive MongoDB, Cassandra, R2DBC for databases. WebClient for non-blocking HTTP calls. Reactive WebSockets. Functional endpoints with RouterFunctions. Backpressure handling. Better scalability for I/O-bound applications with fewer threads. Netty is the default embedded server for WebFlux.
